A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The text, equations, Table 1, Figures 1–10, and Appendices A–K are available and support reliable comparison despite the layout change.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix K report original synthetic retrieval experiments, including accuracy gaps, attention maps, and attention-sink measurements.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix K retain the work's original synthetic retrieval experiments and attention-sink results.

M1.justification: The attention-update equations, graph-based framework, masking mechanisms, positional encodings, and experimental network architecture are retained. The added attention-rollout discussion identifies a connection to existing work without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture retrieval task, novel-class evaluation, and unbiased or position-biased synthetic sequences. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains No PE, decay mask, and RoPE comparisons. Figures 3–6 retain no-mask versus causal-mask comparisons under No PE, sinusoidal PE, and RoPE. Appendix K.2 retains the same causal, sliding-window, and prefix-mask configurations.

E3.justification: Appendix J revises the stated decay-mask parameter from m = 0.8 to m = −log(0.8) ≈ 0.223. This is a reported setting change; the PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun. The remaining sample sizes, metrics, model configurations, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: The depth and positional-encoding analysis, training-position-bias experiments, and attention-sink analyses are retained in Section 5 and Appendix K. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five runs in Sections 5.1–5.2. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2–10 retain identical plotted results and qualitative findings. For example, Figure 2's No PE first-versus-last gaps remain 0.053, 0.092, and 0.120 at depths 2, 6, and 10. The revised stated decay parameter does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Lemmas 4.4 and 4.6 and Theorems 4.5 and 4.7 now explicitly restrict their bounds to j ≤ i ∈ [N], clarifying that they concern permitted causal-attention entries. The bound formulas, assumptions A1–A3, and substantive proofs in Appendices A–I remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about causal masking, depth-dependent early-position bias, competing positional-encoding effects, and synthetic empirical validation. Removing the adjective 'novel' does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly identifies interactions with value projections and MLPs as an extension requiring further analysis, citing vector-norm-based work. This adds a concrete qualification to the framework's scope; existing interpretations of retrieval bias and attention sinks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a code-repository access footnote, and Appendix J revises the documented decay-mask hyperparameter. Existing data-generation details, PyTorch implementation information, V100 hardware, optimizer settings, and training duration are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Abnar and Zuidema (2020), explicitly identifying the analyzed quantity with attention rollout while distinguishing its theoretical use. It also adds Kobayashi et al. (2020) and broadens introductory attribution to existing graph-based attention analyses. These are focused positioning changes.

P1.justification: The section and appendix organization is retained. Local edits add the attention-rollout paragraph, expand the conclusion, introduce acknowledgements and an impact statement, and correct Section 5.2's reference from Figure 1 to Figure 2. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout, substantially reflowing equations, tables, figures, and captions. Running headers and appendix spacing also change. Table 1 and all ten figure graphics are retained rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 improves attribution through the attention-rollout discussion, supplies code-access information, and more clearly identifies extensions beyond the current analysis. These are useful but limited improvements because the empirical evidence and substantive proofs are retained. The decay-parameter revision is not accompanied by evidence of rerunning experiments, so it does not establish improved empirical validity.
